summary: The direction parametrization, cap splines, slice-mass formula, slope breakpoints, tails, and stationary equation are otherwise consistent. However, the affine area normalization is not stated consistently, and the claimed polynomial reduction contains a false denominator assertion and omits necessary degeneracy and boundary cases after eliminating the slope.
critical_errors: After replacing the triangle by conv{0,e1,e2}, its Euclidean area is 1/2, whereas D was defined as the area before the affine change. Thus the displayed definition Φ(t)=area{u∈Δ:L(u)≤t}/D does not yield Φ(t)=1 above the largest knot unless D=1/2. The proof informally retains the original factor D but never defines a pulled-back area measure or redefines D, so (5)-(9) do not follow literally from the stated definition.

Solving the linear stationary equation (14) can introduce denominators other than powers of ρ and 1−ρ, contrary to the final paragraph. For example, when the bottom term is on the lower quadratic branch and the top term is on the upper quadratic branch, stationarity has the form (1−2ρ)σ=ρ[λ2(γ+1)−λ1m]−(1−ρ)[λ1m−λ0γ]. Hence the substituted candidate generally has a denominator 1−2ρ, which changes sign and vanishes inside (0,1); multiplying only by positive powers of ρ and 1−ρ does not clear all denominators while preserving feasibility.
gaps: After substituting an interior stationary slope, the feasible ρ-domain also has boundaries where that slope meets a spline breakpoint, σ*(ρ)=B_{i,k}(ρ), and where the coefficient of σ in (14) vanishes. These cases are not among regimes 1-6, nor is there an argument showing that their values are necessarily recovered by the separately optimized breakpoint systems. Consequently the asserted completeness of the finite system list is not proved.
repair_hints: State explicitly whether area after normalization is the pulled-back original area measure, or normalize by the area of the transformed triangle and then use affine invariance of all ratios.

Avoid dividing by the coefficient of σ: retain ρ and σ as variables and impose the two polynomialized first-order equations, with separate treatment of coefficient-zero cases. Alternatively, split by the sign and zero set of every introduced denominator.
Include stationary-to-breakpoint contact equations, or prove carefully that any global minimum at such a contact is captured by a breakpoint candidate and its own boundary or stationary equations.
